newsitem.title: USA: Marvin Davis offers $835 million for Carter-Wallace.
newsitem.headline: Marvin Davis offers $835 million for Carter-Wallace.

text.p: Carter-Wallace Inc., a maker of consumer and health-care products such as condoms and deodorants, said Wednesday that billionaire investor Marvin Davis has offered to buy the company in deal estimated to be worth $835 million.

In a statement, the company said that it received a letter from Davis Companies stating that Davis is prepared to negotiate the acquisition of all outstanding shares of Carter-Wallace for $18 a share.
Following the news, Carter-Wallace's stock jumped $4.25 to $16 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Carter-Wallace, which makes Trojan condoms and Arrid deodorants, has 46.39 million shares outstanding, which would value the acquisition at $835 million.
Los Angeles-based Davis Companies is a closely held company owned by Davis.
Carter-Wallace said it referred the letter to CPI Development Corp., its majority stockolder.
